reason: The goal calls for supplying muscle fibers, and sugar is identified as fuel.
expectation: The fibers will receive sugar, possibly along with the available oxygen.

effect: The fibers have begun breaking down sugar and producing some ATP; oxygen still appears needed for the supply goal.
reaction: The picture makes the first stage of fuel processing clear, and I’m curious what oxygen adds.
reason: Oxygen is the other supply named in the goal, and the sugar-processing fibers are ready for it.
expectation: The fibers will use oxygen to continue processing fuel and make more ATP.

effect: Oxygen completed the supply goal, and the ATP cycle shows how the fibers can continue working. The next goal is to collect and transmit their pulls.
reaction: The cycle helps connect fuel and oxygen to muscle work, though “used carrier” is a little abstract.
reason: The connective wrapping is shown fitting around a group of muscle cells, which suggests it can collect their pulls.
expectation: The wrapping will gather the fibers into a muscle structure.

effect: The wrapping gathered the fibers into bundles and showed how their pulls combine; tendons still need attaching.
reaction: The joined arrows make the wrapping’s role clear.
reason: The goal is to transmit the pulls, and the front tendons are described as attachment cords.
expectation: The front tendons will attach to the bundles to transmit their pull.

effect: The front tendons formed a bending muscle group; the rear tendons appear to be the remaining part needed to complete the muscle groups.
reaction: The tendon explanation clarifies why the attachment matters, though the bones are still absent.
reason: The rear tendons appear intended for the remaining muscle bundles.
expectation: The rear tendons will form a second muscle group that can transmit its pull.

effect: The rear tendons formed the straightening muscles and completed the goal of collecting and transmitting the fibers’ pulls.
reaction: It was satisfying to finish the paired muscle groups, though I would have liked to see how they act on bones.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding connective wrapping was most worthwhile: the picture’s arrows showed how individual cell pulls become a larger pull, connecting cellular work to a muscle group.

leastWorthwhile.text: Attaching the rear tendons felt repetitive after attaching the front tendons; the result added little explanation of the difference between the groups.

surprise.text: I was interested that sugar breakdown produced some ATP before oxygen was added, with the remaining fuel pieces continuing toward a mitochondrion.

arbitrary.text: The rear tendon action had a clear purpose, but why this particular set produces straightening muscles was not clear from the supplied descriptions.

continue.text: I would choose to continue because I want to see how the two muscle groups attach to bones and move a joint.
